blocks.heading: A CONVINCING TRAILER IS NOT A GAME
blocks.body:
Fox Stories looked like a complete cozy adventure before that kind of errand-driven game had a familiar genre label. The prototype could be explored and items could be picked up, but the NPC interactions in the trailer were scripted and there was no real stealing, progression or sustaining gameplay loop.

The response was far larger than the prototype deserved. That attention pushed us to ask a harder question on every project afterward: what does the player actually do, and what role or profession lets them belong in the world?

blocks.heading: THE FANTASY TRAVELED FURTHER THAN THE PROTOTYPE
blocks.body: The response was exciting, but it exposed the gap between a world people wanted and a game we knew how to make. I keep the number here as evidence of resonance, not as proof that the design was solved.
